processing.name: Alwar–Bharatpur Industrial Processing Heartland (Rajasthan)
products: Strategic Role: Globally recognized as the primary price-discovery, crushing, and physical assembly center for Indian mustard. Sets daily spot pricing for domestic seed and expeller cakes.
catchment: Catchment Areas: Alwar, Bharatpur, Dausa, Jaipur, Sawai Madhopur, Karauli (Rajasthan); southern Haryana districts (Bhiwani, Mahendragarh, Rewari).

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: Globally recognized as the primary price-discovery, crushing, and physical assembly center for Indian mustard. Sets daily spot pricing for domestic seed and expeller cakes.

Key Facilities: Over 350 mechanized expeller units, solvent extraction plants, and automated tin-filling operations in Alwar (Matsya Industrial Area), Khairthal, Bharatpur, and Jaipur (Vishwakarma & Sitapura Industrial Areas); high-throughput cleaning, destoning, and gravity separation lines.
Catchment Areas: Alwar, Bharatpur, Dausa, Jaipur, Sawai Madhopur, Karauli (Rajasthan); southern Haryana districts (Bhiwani, Mahendragarh, Rewari).

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: Center for commercial edible oil expelling, brand packaging, and inter-state logistics linking central production to northern consumption.

Key Facilities: Historic industrial crushing clusters in Agra (Belanganj & Foundry Nagar) and Kanpur (Fazalganj & Panki Industrial Areas); large modern corporate bottling plants (e.g., B.L. Agro, Adani Wilmar, Patanjali) packaging oil into retail poly-pouches, PET bottles, and 15-kg tin containers.
Catchment Areas: Agra, Mathura, Aligarh, Hathras, Firozabad, Kanpur, Fatehpur (UP); heavy inbound raw seed truck arrivals from the Chambal valley (Morena, Bhind, Sheopur).

summary.text: In Indian agricultural statistics (Directorate of Economics & Statistics / ICAR-DRMR Bharatpur / Solvent Extractors' Association of India), Rapeseed & Mustard (Brassica spp., locally Sarson, Rai, Toria, Tara Mira) is India's most important winter (Rabi) edible oilseed crop. Over recent seasons, it has emerged as the number-one domestic edible oilseed in terms of total oil production, contributing over 30% of total oilseed acreage and approximately 33% to 35% of total vegetable oil production in India. India ranks as the world's third-largest producer after Canada and China.

protection.name: Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Devastating in North & Central India)
protection.impact: Colonies of small, soft-bodied, greenish-yellow aphids cluster on tender shoots, inflorescences, and young siliquae; suck phloem sap; plants become stunted, flowers fail to set pods, and young siliquae shrivel and dry up; exude sticky honeydew that fosters black sooty mold; causes 30–90% yield loss during overcast winter spells.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: White Rust / Blister (Albugo candida)
protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in Rajasthan, Haryana, UP)
protection.impact: Shiny, white-to-creamy raised pustules (blisters) appear on leaf undersides; corresponding upper leaf surfaces show chlorotic yellow patches; systemic floral infection transforms inflorescences into a swollen, fleshy, twisted green structure ("Staghead" gall deformity); completely suppresses seed set; causes 20–50% yield loss.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Alternaria Black Spot / Blight (Alternaria brassicae, A. brassicicola)
protection.geography: Humid Alluvial & Irrigated Belts (Heavy in West Bengal, Assam, UP)
protection.impact: Small, circular brown-to-black spots with distinct concentric rings on leaves, stems, and pods; lesions coalesce into large necrotic blights; causes premature leaf drying, stem snapping, and blackened, shriveled siliquae with under-developed seeds; reduces oil content by 5–10%.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Sclerotinia Stem Rot (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum)
protection.impact: Elongated, water-soaked, bleached, greyish-white lesions appear on the lower main stem; lesions girdle the stem; stem splits open longitudinally, revealing a hollow pith filled with white fungal mycelium and large, hard, jet-black rat-dropping-like sclerotial bodies; plants lodge and dry completely; destroys 30–70% of crop.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Mustard Sawfly (Athalia lugens proxima) & Painted Bug (Bagrada hilaris)
protection.impact:
Sawfly: Dark greenish-black cylindrical larvae feed on seedling leaves, chewing large circular holes; curl into a ring and drop to ground when touched.

Painted Bug: Orange-black shield bugs suck sap from young seedlings, causing wilting; feed on maturing pods, causing chalky, empty seeds.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rust-Red Flour Beetle & Cigarette Beetle (Tribolium castaneum, Lasioderma)
protection.impact: Adult beetles and larvae bore into damaged, broken mustard seeds and expeller cakes; feed on residual endosperm and fats, elevating free fatty acids (FFA) and causing rancidity.
protection.passage: Rapeseed & Mustard — source table 162, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
